paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God tests Abraham, and the test shows Abraham fears God. The angel of the LORD says so himself: "now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your only son from me" (Genesis 22:12). Abraham held nothing back, even the son he loved (Genesis 22:2). I think that's what trust looks like when it costs you something.

Then comes the part that gets me, so hold onto your apron. When Isaac asks where the lamb is, Abraham says, "God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son" (Genesis 22:8). And God does. Abraham looks up and sees a ram caught in a thicket, and he offers it "in place of his son" (Genesis 22:13). Abraham names the place "The LORD Will Provide" (Genesis 22:14), and that's what God's people can lean on when they can't see how it will work out.

The story doesn't stop at the ram, because God keeps giving. He swears by Himself to bless Abraham, and says "through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed" (Genesis 22:18). So the baker gets the same lesson: obey God, and trust Him to provide what you can't. I'm still learning that one myself, friend, even after being pulled out of a junk drawer. And this story isn't over, because there's more to come for Abraham.
